extra_quotes: We performed spin-polarized DFT calculations using the PA W method in V ASP with the PBE functional, a 500 eV plane-wave cutoff, a 9×13×1kmesh, and Dudarev Hubbard parametersU eff = 5.25 eV for Mn and 1.13 eV for Nb, obtained by linear response (Fig. S13).
Finite-displacement phonons were calculated with Phonopy in 2×2×1 supercells, from which the lattice entropy and heat capacity were obtained.
Isotropic exchange and DMI parameters were extracted with the LKAG formalism in TB2J from SIESTA calculations based on the V ASP-relaxed structures.

Together with the orthorhombic anisotropy, these parameters define a classical spin Hamiltonian, which was simulated with V AMPIRE to obtain the Curie temperatures, field- and temperature-dependent magnetization, and magnetic heat capacity.

For NbMnSe 2, SOC-included bands were mapped onto maximally localized Wannier functions comprising Mn and Nb dand Seporbitals. Conductivities were then calculated with WannierTools using the semiclassical Boltzmann equation in the constant-relaxation-time approximation and a 111×171×1 mesh.

These comparisons do not by themselves establish a synthesis route, but together with the phonon and finite-temperature tests they show that the predicted magnetic states occur in well-defined metastable monolayers rather than mechanically unstable structures.

This endpoint interpolation does not replace an explicit finite-temperature spin–phonon calculation, but it isolates the leading thermodynamic consequence of the calculated entropy difference between the ordered and disordered magnetic states.
This estimate characterizes the anisotropy-energy scale rather than a coercive field, which will depend on the actual switching pathway and domain structure.
